text: Lemma N1 [on paper]. $J_k=\mathrm{span}\{\mu(r)-1:r\in R_0\}+\sum_j\big(J_{k-1}a_j+a_jJ_{k-1}\big)$, the products taken in $A_k$ (also modulo $2^E$). Proof. For $z\in J_{k-1}$ take a lift $\tilde z\in J_k$; $\tilde z a_j=za_j$ in $A_k$ because the degree-$(k-1)$ part of $\tilde z$ dies in the product; so "$\supseteq$". Conversely $J_k$ is spanned by $u(\mu(r)-1)v$ with monomials $u,v$; if $v=v'a_j$, then $u(\mu(r)-1)v=\big(u(\mu(r)-1)v'\big)a_j$ and the bracket is in $J_k$, its truncation in $J_{k-1}$; the same on the left. $\square$
